topic.title: Neural Speech Recognition and Temporal Acoustic Modeling
topic.overview: Speech recognition maps changing acoustic signals to linguistic categories while coping with timing, speakers, accents, and limited data. This cluster strongly features early combinations of neural discriminators with hidden Markov models, where learned acoustic probabilities and structured temporal decoding perform different roles. Newer representatives revisit robustness and coverage of underserved speech varieties.
topic.whyItMatters: Better frame classification does not automatically improve whole-word recognition. A useful system must combine local evidence consistently over time and avoid cascading errors when an accent or language is unfamiliar.
topic.evolution: Late-1980s work explores temporal state representations and neural emission estimates for Markov models. The 1990s representatives refine hybrid recognition and feature extraction. Recent datasets and low-resource language-detection methods emphasize linguistic diversity, while a speech-first position paper argues for broader research priorities. These later concerns expand evaluation rather than erase the earlier temporal-modeling problem.
openQuestions: How can low-resource systems distinguish accent variation from a change of language?
Which acoustic representations preserve timing cues needed beyond transcription?

papers.tldr: wav2vec-U combines self-supervised speech representations and adversarial training to achieve strong speech recognition without labeled training data.

papers.title: ContentVec: An Improved Self-Supervised Speech Representation by Disentangling Speakers
papers.tldr: ContentVec regularizes HuBERT’s teacher labels and learned representations to reduce speaker information without severe content loss, improving evaluated content-focused speech tasks.

papers.title: Self-supervised learning with random-projection quantizer for speech recognition
papers.tldr: A fixed random-projection quantizer supplies effective masked-prediction targets for self-supervised speech recognition.

papers.title: Global Normalization for Streaming Speech Recognition in a Modular Framework
papers.tldr: GNAT makes exact global normalization tractable and reduces the streaming versus non-streaming word error rate gap by over 50% on Librispeech.

papers.title: Losses Can Be Blessings: Routing Self-Supervised Speech Representations Towards Efficient Multilingual and Multitask Speech Processing
papers.tldr: S³-Router adapts speech-model connections, reporting better accuracy than weight fine-tuning while removing at most 10% of weights.

papers.title: Star Temporal Classification: Sequence Modeling with Partially Labeled Data
papers.tldr: STC uses a wildcard-like star token to train sequence models when labels are missing and unaligned.

papers.title: Efficient Sequence Transduction by Jointly Predicting Tokens and Durations
papers.tldr: TDT predicts tokens and their durations together, enabling frame skipping that improves reported inference speed and accuracy.

papers.title: Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision
papers.tldr: Speech models trained on 680,000 hours of multilingual, multitask supervision generalize well without dataset-specific fine-tuning and approach human performance in reported comparisons.

papers.title: Self-supervised Neural Factor Analysis for Disentangling Utterance-level Speech Representations
papers.tldr: Factor analysis adds disentangled utterance representations and a training objective that improve non-semantic speech tasks with limited labels.

papers.title: DinoSR: Self-Distillation and Online Clustering for Self-supervised Speech Representation Learning
papers.tldr: DinoSR turns a teacher network's audio representations into clustered speech units that supervise a student, improving several downstream tasks.

papers.title: Disentangling Voice and Content with Self-Supervision for Speaker Recognition
papers.tldr: A self-supervised disentanglement framework separates speaker traits from speech content and improves reported speaker-recognition measures.

papers.title: Speech Self-Supervised Learning Using Diffusion Model Synthetic Data
papers.tldr: DiffS4L improves speech self-supervised learning by supplementing limited recordings with diffusion-generated audio containing new acoustic and content variation.

papers.title: BIGOS V2 Benchmark for Polish ASR: Curated Datasets and Tools for Reproducible Evaluation
papers.tldr: BIGOS V2 organizes public speech datasets and open tools into a large, reproducible benchmark for Polish speech recognition.

papers.title: General Detection-based Text Line Recognition
papers.tldr: Synthetic pretraining and joint character detection enable parallel text-line recognition with line-level fine-tuning annotations.

papers.title: Language Without Borders: A Dataset and Benchmark for Code-Switching Lip Reading
papers.tldr: CSLR provides a large Chinese-English lip-reading dataset and benchmark for sentences that switch between languages.

papers.title: Muharaf: Manuscripts of Handwritten Arabic Dataset for Cursive Text Recognition
papers.tldr: Muharaf provides over 1,600 historical Arabic manuscript pages with expert transcriptions, spatial annotations, and a preliminary recognition baseline.

papers.title: REBORN: Reinforcement-Learned Boundary Segmentation with Iterative Training for Unsupervised ASR
papers.tldr: REBORN alternates reinforcement-learned speech segmentation with phoneme prediction, improving unsupervised recognition across the reported language benchmarks.

papers.title: Separate and Reconstruct: Asymmetric Encoder-Decoder for Speech Separation
papers.tldr: Early speaker-feature separation and global-local Transformer processing improve speech separation while reducing computation in the reported benchmarks.

papers.title: SSDM: Scalable Speech Dysfluency Modeling
papers.tldr: SSDM combines new alignment methods, a large simulated dysfluency corpus, and an LLM-based system for scalable speech dysfluency modeling.

papers.title: Topic-Conversation Relevance (TCR) Dataset and Benchmarks
papers.tldr: TCR supplies diverse meeting transcripts, topics, augmentation tools, and GPT-4 benchmarks for evaluating conversation relevance.

papers.title: EuroSpeech: A Multilingual Speech Corpus
papers.tldr: EuroSpeech converts parliamentary recordings into over 61,000 hours of multilingual speech data and substantially improves evaluated speech recognition performance.

papers.title: RESPIN-S1.0: A read speech corpus of 10000+ hours in dialects of nine Indian Languages
papers.tldr: RESPIN-S1.0 provides over 10,000 hours of clean read speech across nine Indian languages and more than 38 dialects, improving recognition through fine-tuning.

papers.title: SeniorTalk: A Chinese Conversation Dataset with Rich Annotations for Super-Aged Seniors
papers.tldr: SeniorTalk supplies richly annotated Chinese conversations from adults aged 75 and above to support research on speech technologies for older users.

papers.title: The Omni-Expert: A Computationally Efficient Approach to Achieve a Mixture of Experts in a Single Expert Model
papers.tldr: The Omni-Expert uses feature transformations to deliver efficient specialization in a single model for cochlear-implant speech dereverberation.

papers.title: Time-Masked Transformers with Lightweight Test-Time Adaptation for Neural Speech Decoding
papers.tldr: Extensive time masking, a compact Transformer, and one-step test-time adaptation improve real-time neural speech decoding while reducing computation.

papers.title: WolBanking77: Wolof Banking Speech Intent Classification Dataset
papers.tldr: WolBanking77 introduces Wolof banking text and speech data with baseline evaluations for intent classification and speech recognition.

papers.title: Convex Low-resource Accent-Robust Language Detection in Speech Recognition
papers.tldr: CLD uses convex optimization to improve language detection under limited data and accent variation, with theoretical stability guarantees and reported accuracy of 97–98%.

papers.title: Position: The Text-Centric Bias in Foundation Models Must Be Revisited for a Speech-First Future
papers.tldr: The authors urge speech-native model development, arguing that changing interaction habits will shift future data distributions toward audio.
